notes: demo(UserGuide13), section 13.3 of the MLwiN User's Guide (Rasbash et al. 2012), whose first lines are the help page's example: reading1[reading1 == -10] <- NA sets the code -10 missing in every read and age column, then reshape(direction = "long") stacks read1 to read6 and age1 to age6 over the six occasions, renamed reading and age, and runMLwiN(reading ~ 1 + age + (1 + age | student) + (1 | occasion)) fits the linear growth curve. R2MLwiN names the level-1 unit in the formula, so (1 | occasion) is the residual, which lme4 leaves implicit. The demo numbers the pupils as student, its timevar overwriting id; id, the unique pupil code, names each wide row once and groups the rows alike. Section 13.2 fits the null model (a fixed-effects version); sections 13.4 and 13.5 let the level-1 variance depend on age and add I(age^2) to both parts, which lme4 cannot state. Hand check #210: two readings differed on the model, and the outside check takes section 13.3's linear growth curve, the last fit of the chapter that lme4 states in full, over section 13.5's quadratic curve, whose residual variance changes with age.

formula: dep ~ pre + group + I(month - 1) + (1 + I(month - 1) | subj)
notes: The publisher's solution to MLMUS4 exercise 6.2 (postnatal-depression data; mlmus4-vol1-solutions.pdf and its ex6_2_postnatal.do) reshapes as here (reshape long dep, i(subj) j(month)) and, after "Missing values for the depression scores are coded as -9 in the dataset", runs mvdecode dep pre, mv(-9), whose output reports 71 missing values in dep and none in pre, so only dep declares the code. It sets time = month - 1 and fits mixed dep pre group time || subj: time, covariance(unstructured) mle, the random-coefficient model a likelihood-ratio test prefers to the random intercept (step 7). Its other models put unstructured, exchangeable, AR(1) or Toeplitz structures on the residuals, which lme4 cannot state: by AIC the unstructured residuals are best, by BIC the random intercept with AR(1) residuals, then this model. group (0 or 1) and pre, the score before the six months, are constant within subj; the dropout is monotone.

formula: deaths ~ semi-mechanistic renewal-equation epidemic model (f, SI, x); country-specific R0 mu, seeded infections y and IFR noise
documented_prior: tau ~ exponential(0.03); y ~ exponential(1 / tau); phi ~ normal(0, 5); kappa ~ normal(0, 0.5); mu ~ normal(3.28, kappa); alpha_hier ~ gamma(.1667, 1); ifr_noise ~ normal(1, 0.1)
notes: NONLINEAR: covid19imperial_v2.stan, identical to v3 (Flaxman et al. 2020; posteriordb's two posteriors on this data), seeds each country's infections by y[m] for N0 days, renews them over the serial interval SI with Rt = mu[m] * exp(-X[m] * alpha) scaled by the susceptible share of pop[m], convolves them with f times ifr_noise[m] into expected deaths and fits deaths[EpidemicStart[m]:N[m], m] ~ neg_binomial_2(E_deaths, phi). The country-level mu ~ normal(3.28, kappa), y ~ exponential(1 / tau) and ifr_noise ~ normal(1, 0.1) make country the grouping factor. The data dict's deaths[N2, M], cases and f set the stack: country 1 to 14 from the column suffixes (the data names no country), x numbering the days 1 to N2, so the countries are the occasions and the days the wide rows. The Stan comment "the rows with i > N contain -1 and should be ignored" documents deaths=-1, and the Imperial code the model's info links (covid19model base.r) pads cases alike with rep(-1, forecast). cases enters no term (ignored); cases_4 holds one negative daily count on an observed day, a reporting revision, not a code. RULE GAP: the interventions X (a country by day by 6 array), pop, N and EpidemicStart are no columns, and the likelihood skips the days before EpidemicStart (31 for every country), which enter only through the seeding. ecdc0401 is this table cut at 2020-04-01, excluded as its copy.
